text:
sasha: Quick follow-up from the penalty-matrix RFC — found some practical interop gaps between admission and quota v2 when we tried a staged rollout.

raj: ugh, details?

sasha: two main issues: 1) different semantics for 'soft' vs 'hard' penalties (quota v2 treated soft as advisory in some codepaths), 2) rounding/quantization of penalty weights caused tie-break flakiness during bursts.

anna: can you paste the failing case? small repro helps.

sasha: repro in dev: single tenant -> concurrent low-qps probes + a short unthrottled burst. admission applied soft penalty 0.2, quota v2 stored 0.1999999 and admission compared >=0.2 so it fell through.

kevin: floating-point ops? we should normalize to int milli-penalty. agreed we need canonical representation. :thumbsup:

sec-oncall: is this causing customer-visible errors or just internal metric noise?

sasha: mostly internal but leads to incorrect fallback to conservative path during heavy bursts, which increases 95p latency for a subset of requests. not a data leak or security issue.

raj: two immediate fixes: 1) canonicalize penalty encoding on the wire (proto change) 2) admission should use tolerant comparison with epsilon for existing runtimes.

lucy: proto change will be breaking for older agents unless we add a compatibility flag. we could add a new field penalty_milli to the proto and keep legacy penalty_float for now.

kevin: +1 to penalty_milli, but let's also version the field so rollouts can be phased. update the decoder to prefer milli when present.

anna: for tie-break randomness: rounding to milli will reduce ties but we still need deterministic tie-breaker to avoid oscillation. suggest (tenant_id hash xor epoch) as last resort.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging rollout started for quota-v2 (canary=10% traffic) — watch quota-ingest errors.

raj: ops-bot noted. we should also add an e2e test in admission-integration that simulates float-edge cases. low effort.

sasha: proposed plan: A) add penalty_milli in proto + decoder fallback (owner: lucy) B) admission tolerant-compare patch (owner: raj) C) deterministic tie-breaker added to admission reward function (owner: anna) D) e2e test and canary flush (owner: kevin) E) doc note for SRE runbook (owner: sec-oncall).

kevin: timeline?

sasha: aiming for small PRs this week, canary next Tue, full rollout Thu if stable.

lucy: I'll open proto PR and include migration notes. will ping perf team for microbench.

anna: will draft deterministic tie-breaker pseudo in this thread later today.

raj: i'll do the tolerant-compare, small change. will add unit tests.

sec-oncall: once PRs land, add a short monitor: new metric admission.penalty_mismatch_count and an alert threshold (e.g. > 5/min on canary).

sasha: good. also flag to watch: any increase in observed latency 95/99 on canary tenants. set baseline now.

kevin: I'll add the canary dashboard and a synthetic probe that fires the burst case every 30s.

sasha: thanks all. leaving action items in #eng-security-board as checklist. will follow up with links once PRs are up. :white_check_mark:

lucy: quick note: proto change will require regenerating client stubs; I'll add a compat test in CI.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary health checks passing so far (0 errors / 5m).

anna: nits: mention in runbook to rollback penalty_milli if agents fail to decode (grace period).

sasha: noted. ok i'll close this thread once PRs are green. thanks!
